title: Choose the portfolio's visual world
question: A pale research folio with scroll-scrubbed dither specimens, an alternate, or a re-roll?

options.label: Pale Specimen Ledger
options.lineage: field-research folios, microscope contact sheets, and dithered motion studies
options.thesis: A white field ledger where Kuan Yi's work is encountered as a sequence of live, glitching specimens.
options.viewport: A sparse nameplate and one animated llama specimen dominate an open white field; a precise line of text leads into the scroll.
options.risk: Needs disciplined copy and generous silence so the experimental motion never becomes visual noise.

options.label: Layered Paper Cut
options.thesis: Each project appears as a colored layer added to a folded composition.
options.viewport: A symmetrical cut-out form opens around a personal introduction.
options.risk: Fuses poorly with the requested glitch-image behavior; it would soften the technical, pixel-based character.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.thesis: A full-screen generated field turns each project into a spatial world.
options.viewport: A reactive scene fills the screen behind a minimal introduction.
options.risk: Fuses poorly with the required pale, text-led restraint and can obscure professional proof.

options.label: Field Poster Series
options.thesis: The portfolio becomes a progression of bold travel-style posters for each pursuit.
options.viewport: A single illustrated pursuit occupies the page above a concise imperative.
options.risk: Identifies with golf and exploration, but flattens the research and moving-image aspects into illustration.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A quiet, impeccable personal portfolio in the Ben Lafferty vein.
canonCard.viewport: Text-led introduction, concise project list, and clear contact links on a pale canvas.
